_notes.summary: Defines how the bot generates one scenario per planet at beat open. Scenarios are produced by template-driven randomisation — no LLM required. Each scenario has: codename (2 words), narrative (1-2 sentences), dominant_tags (2 doctrine tags), terminus_intel (known|suspected|none), pressure_modifier (int), and mission_bias (2 mission IDs).
_notes.when_generated: At beat open, after the Watch Master's planet pick window opens. Bot generates one scenario per node: the current committed node + all adjacent nodes (from jericho_reach_graph.json edges, bidirectional). Scenarios are stored in campaign_state.beat_scenarios and presented to the Watch Master during his cascade window.
generation_pipeline: 2. For each node: determine base_dominant_tags from node_type_affinity + region_modifier.
3. Apply pressure modifier — high pressure pushes terminus/suppression into dominant_tags.
4. Determine terminus_intel level from pressure + node_type terminus_affinity.
5. Compute pressure_modifier for the scenario (what committing here does to this node's pressure).
6. Select mission_bias from tag → mission table.
7. Select codename: pick one word from each of the two codename_pools matching dominant_tags. Randomise within pool.
8. Select narrative: pick one template from narrative_templates matching node_type. Fill placeholders.
_notes.randomisation: All selection within pools is seeded with (campaign_id + beat + node_id) for reproducibility — the same scenario is always generated for the same campaign/beat/node combination. This prevents scenarios changing if the bot restarts.

node_type_affinity._note: Three threat vectors per node type. Each vector is a distinct doctrinal angle the WM can commit to. The bot generates all three per node at beat open; the WM picks one, locking that vector's tags as the beat's dominant_tags. base_tags is kept for backward-compat fallback (= vector A tags).

region_modifier._note: Applies an additional tag push on top of node_type_affinity. Does not replace — it pushes pressure toward one tag in the dominant pair or substitutes the secondary.

acheros_salient.note: Chaos-contested. Everything here is contested, everything escalates.

orpheus_salient.note: Under sustained assault. The salient is being rolled back — endurance is the watchword.

iron_collar.note: The fortified ring. These worlds hold or everything behind them falls.

quarantined.note: Corrupted or xenos-saturated. Quarantine designation means the warp is a factor.

hadex.note: Near the Hadex Anomaly. Terminus threats are elevated across this region.

black_reef.note: The Reef worlds — void-hidden, difficult approach, surgical operations only.

canis_salient.note: Active warzone salient — sustained horde-level pressure.

cellebos_warzone.note: Warzone — take ground or lose it.

slinnar_drift.note: The Drift — uncertain space, shifting threat profiles.

pressure_rules._note: How node pressure modifies dominant_tags and terminus_intel at scenario generation time.
pressure_rules.note: +1_step means: if base was 'none' → 'suspected'. If base was 'suspected' → 'known'. 'known' cannot go higher. force_known overrides regardless of base.

terminus_intel_base._note: Base terminus_intel level before pressure modifier. Derived from node_type terminus_affinity.
terminus_intel_base.medium: none → suspected (50/50 random, seeded by node+beat)
terminus_intel_base.known: known (always — used for special node types like The Blood Trinity)

pressure_modifier_table._note: What committing to this node does to its pressure. This is the scenario-level pressure_modifier field — not the same as current pressure. Represents what the Watch's presence achieves if they commit ops here.
pressure_modifier_table.note: Negative = pressure reduced (securing). Zero = engagement ongoing, no net pressure gain from Watch presence alone. Positive modifier not used at scenario level — pressure increase is applied when Watch does NOT commit to a node.

mission_bias_table._note: Given a scenario's two dominant_tags, which missions are most appropriate as prestige missions / campaign log context. Bot picks top-2 from the matching tag combos. Mission IDs from operations.json.
mission_bias_table.note: If dominant_tag pair not in table, check both orderings. If neither matches, use fallback. Operations: 1=Inferno, 2=Decapitation, 3=Vox Liberatis, 5=Fall of Atreus, 6=Ballistic Engine, 7=Termination, 8=Obelisk, 9=Exfiltration, 10=Vortex, 11=Reclamation, 12=Disruption, 13=Purgation, 14=Siege.

codename_pools._note: Codenames are two words: ADJECTIVE + NOUN. Bot picks one word from each list whose associated doctrine tags overlap with the scenario's dominant_tags. If no match, falls back to the default pools.

narrative_templates._note: One narrative template is selected per node type. Placeholders: {node} = node display name, {pressure} = current pressure integer, {region} = region display name. Bot picks randomly from the matching node_type list, seeded by campaign+beat+node for reproducibility.
war_world: The front on {node} has not moved in six days. Both sides know it will not hold. The Watch ends the stalemate.
{node} has been a kill zone since the third month. The Tyranid vanguard runs the same approaches on rotation — the Watch breaks the cycle.
Four companies of line infantry have bled out on {node}'s plains. The Watch does not bleed — it cuts.
dead_world: {node} was cleared six years ago. Something has moved back in. The Scribe's auguries are not encouraging.
The ruins of {node} are not empty. They have not been empty for some time. The Watch finds out why.
Dead worlds do not send distress signals. {node} did. Three days ago. The Watch answers.
shrine_world: The pilgrim roads to {node} have gone quiet. The shrines still stand — but the priests will not say what walks the reliquary districts after dark.
{node}'s confessor-houses have been broadcasting the same litany on loop for eleven days. No human is transmitting it.
Blessed ground does not stay blessed without defenders. {node} has not had defenders for three weeks. The Watch remedies this.
fortress_world: The garrison on {node} has not reported casualties in four days. They are not winning — they have stopped counting.
{node}'s walls are intact. The garrison is not. The Watch reinforces what can still hold.
The fortress at {node} was built to endure for centuries. It will not last another week without intervention.
hive_world: {node}'s lower hab-blocks are no longer responding to sector authority. What replaces them is not friendly.
Population pressure on {node} is being weaponised — not by the Tyranids, by something that knows how to use crowds as cover.
The spires of {node} are still lit. The lower city is not. Something has claimed the dark between levels and is working upward.
agri_world: The harvest plains of {node} feed six sectors. The Huntmaster's auguries have something large on the plains. The Watch identifies and removes it.
{node}'s supply lines are cut. Not by accident — by something that knew which lines mattered. The Watch traces the source.
If {node} falls dark, three hundred thousand troops in the {region} go hungry within a month. The Watch does not let that happen.
forge_world: The machine spirits of {node} have been answering queries with the wrong liturgies for nine days. The Forgemaster wants to know what replaced them.
{node}'s production output dropped 40% without any recorded system failure. The silence from the adepts is more alarming than the loss.
Something is using {node}'s manufacturing capability. The Omnissiah's servants are not currently in a position to object.
feral_world: The indigenous tribes of {node} do not retreat. They have been retreating for two weeks. The Watch finds what pushed them back.
Feral worlds produce warriors. {node} has stopped. The hunting parties go out and do not return. The Watch goes in.
The apex of {node} is not native to this world. The Huntmaster has flagged it. The Watch hunts it.
mining_world: The deep tunnels of {node} have been sealed for three years. Something has unsealed them from the inside.
{node}'s extraction teams stopped transmitting from shaft nine eleven days ago. What came up from shaft nine is still active.
The ore shipments from {node} have been arriving — but the workers who send them have not been heard from since the third consignment.
frontier_world: {node} has no established threat profile. That is the problem. The Watch goes in without intelligence and comes back with it.
The Watch has never operated on {node}. That ends this beat — whatever is there now belongs to the record.
First contact on {node} went poorly for the scouting teams. The Watch determines what 'poorly' means and corrects it.
pleasure_world: The luxuries of {node} mask something. They always do. The Watch removes the mask.
Three Watch Keepers disappeared on {node} eight months ago. Their last reports mentioned a subsector of the city that does not appear on official maps.
{node}'s ruling class has been very cooperative with the Watch. Suspiciously so. The Watch finds out what they are hiding.
penal_world: The warden-complex on {node} has stopped responding. The inmates have not stopped broadcasting.
Containment on {node} was rated for one century. It has been forty-six years. Something found the tolerances.
The penitents of {node} were considered contained. The Chaos element among them was not. The Watch excises it.
watch_station: Watch Station {node} has not acknowledged the standard hailing pattern for six days. The Watch investigates its own.
Something boarded {node} three weeks ago. The automated defences are still active — which means whatever boarded them is inside the perimeter.
The station logs from {node} are intact. The station crew is not. The Watch finds out what the logs do not say.
special: {node} defies classification. The Reach's wounds do not follow standard threat doctrine. Neither does the Watch response.
The Void Warden's auguries regarding {node} have been consistent for twelve days: something is finishing. The Watch ensures it does not.
{node} is what happens when the Hadex Anomaly reaches a point in the Reach and twists it. The Watch cuts it before it spreads.

generation_steps.2_region_push: orpheus_salient pushes resilience — secondary tag becomes resilience (replaces recovery in dominant pair, recovery falls to background)
generation_steps.3_effective_dominant_tags: [aggressive, resilience] — but wait: pressure=1 applies no push. Final: [aggressive, resilience]
generation_steps.4_terminus_intel_base: agri_world terminus_affinity = medium → 50/50. Seeded by Aurum+beat1 → rolls 'suspected'
generation_steps.6_mission_bias: aggressive+resilience not in table → check aggressive+recovery (fallback pair): not listed. Check _fallback: [1, 7] = Inferno, Termination. Use [1, 7].
generation_steps._note: In the actual worked example we used aggressive+terminus as dominant tags to make it more dramatic — that could occur if the bot rolls the terminus_intel as 'suspected' and then pushes the secondary tag from resilience to terminus (a valid interpretation of the pressure+terminus_affinity interaction). The final tags are scenario-generation design choices with bounded randomisation, not pure determinism — the seed controls which option within a valid range is picked.
generation_steps.7_codename: aggressive → adjectives: [IRON, SCORCHED, BURNING...] → seeded pick: SCORCHED. recovery → nouns: [HARVEST, SALVAGE...] → seeded pick: HARVEST. Codename: SCORCHED HARVEST.
generation_steps.8_narrative: agri_world templates, seeded pick #1: 'The harvest plains of {node} feed six sectors. The Huntmaster's auguries have something large on the plains. The Watch identifies and removes it.' → filled: 'The harvest plains of Aurum feed six sectors...'

output_scenario.narrative: The harvest plains of Aurum feed six sectors. The Huntmaster's auguries have something large on the plains. The Watch identifies and removes it.
